questions.question: In international investment law, how did the arbitral tribunal in Tecmed v. Mexico (2003) characterize the scope of the 'Fair and Equitable Treatment' (FET) standard regarding investor expectations?
options: It requires the host state to act in a manner that is completely transparent and consistent, providing a predictable legal framework upon which the investor relied when making its investment.
It restricts FET breaches exclusively to instances of gross negligence, egregious bad faith, or clear denial of justice under the traditional Neer standard.
It holds that any post-investment legislative amendment reducing investor profits automatically breaches FET under international customary law.
It obligates the host state to guarantee a absolute regulatory freeze unless the investor consents in writing to statutory modifications.

questions.question: In Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Bosnia and Herzegovina v. Serbia and Montenegro, 2007), what legal test did the International Court of Justice (ICJ) establish for inferring the specific intent (dolus specialis) of genocide from a pattern of conduct?
options: Genocidal intent can be inferred if it is one of several plausible explanations for the acts committed.
Genocidal intent may only be inferred from a pattern of conduct if that intent is the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from the acts in question.
Genocidal intent is automatically presumed whenever targeted civilian casualties exceed a defined numerical threshold.
Genocidal intent cannot be inferred from conduct under any circumstances; explicit written or testimonial evidence from top leadership is required.

questions.question: Under the jurisprudence of the European Court of Human Rights regarding extraterritorial jurisdiction (e.g., Al-Skeini v. United Kingdom), which scenario establishes a jurisdictional link under Article 1 of the ECHR based on 'state agent authority and control'?
options: A state providing generalized financial assistance to foreign non-governmental civil society organizations.
A state voting in favor of a non-binding United Nations General Assembly resolution concerning a third state.
A state's military officials exercising physical power and control over an individual during security operations abroad.
A state granting unilateral official recognition to a newly declared sovereign state without physical presence.

questions.question: Under the 'Monetary Gold' principle established by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), when must the Court decline to exercise its jurisdiction over a dispute between consenting parties?
options: When a non-party state has submitted an application to intervene strictly under Article 62 of the ICJ Statute.
When the subject matter involves diplomatic property claimed by more than two non-aligned sovereign states.
When the legal interpretation of a multilateral treaty affects the non-party state's trade preferences.
When determining the legal responsibility of a non-party state forms the very subject matter of the decision required of the Court.

questions.question: Under Article 64 in conjunction with Article 44(5) of the 1969 Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (VCLT), what is the precise legal consequence for an existing treaty if a new peremptory norm of general international law (jus cogens) emerges?
options: The entire treaty becomes void and terminates, as no severability of treaty provisions is permitted when conflicting with jus cogens.
Only the specific clauses directly in conflict with the new peremptory norm become void, leaving the remainder of the treaty valid.
The treaty remains fully operational, but the parties are granted a five-year grace period to re-negotiate conflicting clauses.
The treaty is suspended indefinitely until the UN General Assembly votes by a two-thirds majority to nullify it.
